input: Draft a monthly client newsletter template

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which sections to include (e.g., company updates, industry news, promotions, case studies) defines the entire structure of the template.
The industry and profile of the clients receiving it directly shapes the language, content relevance, and level of formality.
The platform or tool used to send the newsletter (e.g., Mailchimp, Outlook, Substack) determines the format — HTML, plain text, or a drag-and-drop block layout.
The desired tone (e.g., formal and corporate vs. warm and conversational) changes word choice, greeting style, and overall voice throughout the template.
A target length or word count per section prevents the template from being too dense or too sparse, and guides how much placeholder content to draft.
Understanding the primary goal of the newsletter (e.g., retention, upselling, thought leadership, updates) determines what a successful send looks like and what to emphasise.
Knowing who will fill in the template each month (e.g., a marketing team, a solo founder, an assistant) affects how much guidance, placeholder text, and instructional notes to embed.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a monthly client newsletter template
gold.taskDescription: Create a reusable monthly newsletter template designed to communicate with clients on a regular basis.

questions.title: What sections should the newsletter include each month?
questions.description: Identify the recurring content blocks — such as company news, industry insights, a featured case study, product updates, or a call to action — that must appear in every issue.

questions.title: What industry or type of client will receive this?
questions.description: Clarify the client profile (e.g., B2B tech companies, retail businesses, legal firms) so the language, examples, and content feel directly relevant to the audience.

questions.title: Which platform will you use to send the newsletter?
questions.description: Determine the delivery tool (e.g., Mailchimp, HubSpot, Outlook, Substack) to ensure the template is formatted correctly for that environment.

questions.title: What tone should the newsletter have — formal or conversational?
questions.description: Establish the voice and style of the writing so placeholder copy and structural suggestions consistently reflect the right register for the brand.

questions.title: How long should the total newsletter be per issue?
questions.description: Set a target length (e.g., under 300 words, 500–700 words) so each section's placeholder content is sized appropriately and the template doesn't become unwieldy.

questions.title: What is the main goal you want each issue to achieve?
questions.description: Identify the primary objective — such as improving client retention, driving upsells, building thought leadership, or simply keeping clients informed — to shape what the template emphasises.

questions.title: Who will be filling in the template each month?
questions.description: Know whether a marketing professional, a solo founder, or a non-writer (e.g., an admin assistant) will populate the template, to calibrate how much instructional guidance and example text to embed.
